person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, moving among Dan, Abra, and other characters. The strongest Goodreads passages sustain external narration around Dan and another focal character, while numerous apparent instances of I, we, and you are dialogue, AA-derived material, paratext, gnomic language, or generic address rather than first- or second-person base narration. Scholarly whole-book analysis and an independent explicit point-of-view guide agree that the novel is third-person omniscient. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found; the only residual limitation is that the authorized audio excerpt lacked an accessible transcript.
